item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00066","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C19","C07","C20"],"selected_candidate_label":"C19","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C19 is a near-direct drafting template for the child. It uses the same section 22 authority, the same sequence of Agriculture advice, Tariff Commission investigation and report, presidential findings, a one-year aggregate quota divided between Canada and other countries, and an almost verbatim seed exemption with the same approval-or-bond procedure. The child chiefly substitutes barley and barley malt for oats and changes quantities and weight conversions. C07 and C20 share substantial machinery, especially the seed exemption, but C19 is materially closer in operative structure and phrasing.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"the Secretary of render or tend to render ineffective, or materially interfere with, the price-support program","explanation":"Distinctive recital language is reproduced with the regulated grain changed."},{"child_excerpt":"on August 20, 1954, I caused the United States Tariff Commission to make an investigation under the said section 22 with respect to this matter","parent_excerpt":"on from October 1, 1954, to September 30, 1955... shall not be permitted to exceed 40,000,000 bushels","explanation":"The central quota provision follows the same syntax, annual period, unit, countries","explanation":"Both divide the aggregate grain quota between Canada and all other foreign countries in the same operative sequence."},{"child_excerpt":"The provisions of this proclamation
